top_story: By late 31 July, the sharpest regional shift came in the Gulf: after early indications that Washington and Israel were preparing strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, Iran hit two tankers under U.S. escort in the Strait of Hormuz, pushing the confrontation from signaling toward direct disruption of global shipping and energy flows. The attack raises the likelihood that any U.S.-Israeli response will target economically vital sites, widening civilian exposure through price shocks, maritime risk, and pressure on coastal communities tied to trade. On the same day, Trump cast a Gaza agreement around Hamas disarmament and an IDF withdrawal as a breakthrough, but Israel had not accepted it and far-right Israeli resistance underscored how fragile any pause remains for Palestinians in Gaza. The combined picture is of a region where diplomacy is being outpaced by escalation, leaving local populations to absorb the costs of decisions centered on deterrence and political survival.
